title: Cache & Batch Economics Forecast — Optimize Console Demo w/ Silver Ocean
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Silver Ocean through the Optimize console simulation for batching and prefix/KV caching. We ran through a cost forecast for their chat workload, discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, and agreed to a 2-week sandbox benchmark. Action: share spreadsheet, security pack, and schedule cluster-run test.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm Liam from Redwood. quick roll call?
[00:06] Dana Brooks: Dana here — head of ML at Silver Ocean.
[00:08] Ravi Menon: Ravi, SRE.
[00:10] Evelyn Park: Evelyn for product. Marcus on the call but muted.
[00:15] Priya Rao: Priya, platform SE — i'll drive the demo.
[00:20] Liam Chen: Cool, high level agenda: Optimize console walkthrough, batching/cache recommendations specifically prefix and KV cache, then cost forecast for your typical chat sessions, finally next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Dana Brooks: Yep ev. looking for how we can keep latency under 250ms 95th while lowering token spend — our seq lengths vary lots, some 2-3k for multi-turn.
[00:38] Priya Rao: Got it. quick question on concurrency — what's your typical concurrent sessions?
[00:42] Marcus Li (msg): ~350 peak, average around 120.
[00:46] Priya Rao: thanks. that matters for batching floor.
[00:50] Priya Rao: i'll share my screen — (silence) — ok pulling up the Optimize console: note link in chat https://app.redwood.ai/optimize/sandbox/so-demo
[01:05] Priya Rao: first panel is throughput profile. we uploaded your sample traces (you gave us the 7-day session sample) and the sim ran. you can see sequence length distribution with heavy tail — lots of short completion tokens then a 10% hump around 2k.
[01:20] Ravi Menon: that hump is the multi-turn summary step.
[01:22] Priya Rao: right, so two immediate levers: batching (increase per-GPU tokens/sec) and prefix / KV cache to avoid re-computing prefixes. i'll toggle a scenario: baseline hosted model x-32 fp16 no cache, batch sizing 1-4.
[01:36] [01:36] Priya Rao: baseline P50 token latency 35ms, P95 240ms at your concurrency; cost per 1M tokens $18 (hosted meter).
[01:45] Priya Rao: now enable prefix cache with a 24hr TTL and 30% hit rate (simulated) — big caveat: hit rate depends on sessionization and prompt standardization.
[01:56] Liam Chen: and just to be explicit, our prefix cache is functionally your KV cache, keyed by prefix hash; we store KV states and re-use across sessions when prefix matches. sometimes customers call it session cache or lookahead cache — names vary in docs.
[02:12] Dana Brooks: if we enable that, what happens to latency for misses — is there an added lookup cost?
[02:18] Priya Rao: minimal — lookup is sub-ms; major change is fewer token compute cycles. in this sim, with 30% hit rate, cost per 1M drops to $12.8 and P95 improves slightly to 210ms because a portion of tokens are short-circuit returns.
[02:33] Ravi Menon: 30% seems optimistic; our prompts are pretty customized per customer.
[02:36] Priya Rao: fair — you can tune TTL and canonicalization rules. the console has a prompt-normalization step suggestions (we can share the ruleset). when we simulate 10% hit rate cost is $16.5 per 1M.
[02:48] Evelyn Park: can you show tradeoff table?
[02:50] Priya Rao: yes — table on screen under "Economics". columns: hit rate, avg tokens saved, batch size effect, net cost. example rows: 0% hit => $18, 10% => $16.5, 30% => $12.8, 55% => $9.5. these assume same model family and same throughput profile.
[03:12] Priya Rao: next, batching: we model continuous batching on the runtime; larger batch sizes increase GPU utilization but can add queueing latency. your SLO is 250ms P95 — so we cap effective batch window at 12ms in scenario A.
[03:26] Liam Chen: one note — we also simulate session affinity (keeping KV on same worker) which reduces remote fetches; that helps tail latency.
[03:32] Marcus Li: that seems helpful, but does it require sticky routing that creates imbalance?
[03:36] Priya Rao: it can increase imbalance; the console has a recommended autoscale policy to keep headroom. we can show the predicted 95th-percentile across worst shards.
[03:44] Priya Rao: switching to "Scenario B" — aggressive batching: batch window 40ms, higher utilization; cost drops further to $9.2 per 1M but P95 goes to 420ms, which violates your SLO.
[03:55] Dana Brooks: so the automated suggestion is to use prefix cache first then small batch windows?
[03:59] Priya Rao: usually yes for chat-like with heavy tails. cache reduces compute need, allowing smaller batch windows that meet SLO while saving tokens.
[04:10] Liam Chen: also note quantization options — 8-bit runs can shave another ~18% cost but change quality slightly; we included quality deltas in the console by running eval prompts.
[04:22] Ravi Menon: on security: can caching be done in VPC/private infra?
[04:26] Priya Rao: absolutely — for Redwood Private deployments, KV store can be hosted inside your VPC with KMS integration. we'll attach SOC2 and encryption docs after.
[04:35] Evelyn Park: we need to know retention / purge policy for cache and logs for compliance.
[04:39] Liam Chen: we'll include sample retention configs — default is 30 days but configurable; purge APIs exist and audit logs are available.
[04:46] Priya Rao: back to numbers — i'll open the cost-model spreadsheet live (link: https://redwood.ai/sales/so-sim.xlsx). this is what we'll export for you.
[04:58] [05:00] Priya Rao: ok i'm editing the hit-rate assumption to 15% (more conservative), adjusting concurrency to 350 peak. recalculating...
[05:12] Priya Rao: results: cost per 1M tokens $15.6, annualized estimate for current traffic $64k — compared to baseline $72k. about 13% savings. if you adopt prefix canonicalization to reach 30% then savings jump to ~45%.
[05:29] Dana Brooks: interesting. can you show sensitivity to sequence length? we have a new feature that increases average tokens by 20%.
[05:35] Priya Rao: yes — toggling avg length +20% raises baseline to $86k annual, but cache savings scale proportionally; absolute dollars saved increase but percent savings slightly shrink. short answer: caching still helps but batching/throughput adjustments become more important.
[05:48] Marcus Li: what about dedicated vs hosted? we might prefer reserved pools.
[05:52] Liam Chen: Dedicated (reserved capacity) gives predictable throughput and lower unit compute price if you commit; the console can simulate dedicated pricing vs hosted. for your load, reserved monthly commit yields ~30% unit cost reduction but requires 12-mo commit. we can run a lease vs on-demand calc.
[06:07] Evelyn Park: do you support hybrid? keep sensitive traffic private and burst to hosted?
[06:11] Priya Rao: yes — smart routing policies can route PII or regulated segments to Private, and low-sensitivity burst to hosted. that is in the routing tab.
[06:20] Ravi Menon: latency implications of hybrid?
[06:22] Priya Rao: small — routing decisions add negligible overhead, bigger effects are where the model instance runs (region) and cache locality. we show regional latency heatmaps.
[06:30] Liam Chen: quick check — any immediate blockers on the security side?
[06:33] Dana Brooks: we will need SOC2 gap list and KMS key rotation details.
[06:36] Liam Chen: noted. we'll share security pack and a short architecture note.
[06:40] Priya Rao: demo — i'll create a "playbook" in console that combines: prompt canonicalization rules, 24h TTL, 20% expected hit, batch window 12ms, session affinity on. i'll run sim.
[06:52] Priya Rao: sim results: P95 230ms, cost 14.8/1M, estimated monthly delta -11%.
[07:00] Dana Brooks: ok that's within the SLO envelope. what's the runtime risk at peak?
[07:04] Priya Rao: tail risk is from stragglers; we recommend soft-fallback policy to a smaller model variant that maintains latency at cost of slightly lower quality. the console automates fallback thresholds.
[07:16] Marcus Li: fallback — is that a model swap or quantized variant?
[07:19] Priya Rao: either — you can point a fallback to a cheaper quantized variant or a different model family. it's policy-driven.
[07:27] Ravi Menon: I saw a column "KV storage cost" — what's typical?
[07:30] Priya Rao: small relative to compute — depends on TTL and number of unique prefixes. example: for your distribution at 30% hit and 1M unique prefixes/month, storage is ~ $300-800/month depending on store. compute dominates.
[07:44] Dana Brooks: can we run a controlled benchmark with our traffic?
[07:48] Priya Rao: yes — propose a 2-week sandbox: we deploy an isolated scaffold in your AWS account (or our sandbox), run your replay traces, measure real cache hit rates and tail latency. deliverables: benchmark report, exported spreadsheet, sample configs.
[07:59] Liam Chen: timeline: we can spin sandbox in 3 business days once we get credentials & scope.
[08:04] Evelyn Park: who will own the sandbox?
[08:06] Priya Rao: Redwood SE will run it, and your SRE will provide cluster access or replay traces.
[08:11] Dana Brooks: ok, we need internal signoff but likely green.
[08:14] Liam Chen: great. quick callouts: known limitations — if you have highly personalized prompts per session, prefix cache hit will be low; also canonicalization can introduce small content drift if not carefully validated. we'll include QA steps.
[08:29] Marcus Li: can you show the exported simulation log?
[08:31] Priya Rao: posted in chat: simulation-export.csv (link) — also example charts.
[08:36] Priya Rao: question from Ravi in chat: how do we handle invalidation when user updates context? answer: our KV store supports per-key versioning and a purge API to drop keys for next token. we can also TTL-based invalidation.
[08:49] Ravi Menon: ok. next big question — pricing: is the $/1M number inclusive of cache compute for misses?
[08:56] Priya Rao: yes the model compute includes misses; cache storage and small lookup ops are billed separately on Private deployments, but in hosted tier we bundle lookup ops into unit price. details in pricing sheet.
[09:08] Dana Brooks: team — are there any concerns about vendor lock?
[09:11] Liam Chen: we support standard model formats and offer migration tooling. cache definitions are simple hashed prefixes so they're portable; still, host-specific optimizations may require engineering.
[09:21] Evelyn Park: excellent. let's go over next steps and actions.
[09:25] Liam Chen: recap: Redwood to run 2-week sandbox, share security pack, share simulation spreadsheet, propose a dedicated pricing calc. Silver Ocean to provide replay traces and scope for sandbox, and review canonicalization rules.
[09:40] Dana Brooks: good.
[09:42] Liam Chen: ok that'll be it from us unless other q's?
[09:45] Marcus Li: none.
[09:47] Ravi Menon: all good. thanks.
[09:50] Liam Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invite for sandbox kickoff. bye.
[10:00] [END]
next_steps: Redwood to provision 2-week sandbox and send kickoff invite
Send security pack (SOC2, KMS, retention policies)
Share simulation spreadsheet and canonicalization suggestions
Run commit pricing vs hosted calc and share options
